case_title.quote: Shyamal Ghosh v. State of West Bengal
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment heading.

number_of_accused.quote: Eight accused, namely, Panchanan Tarafdar@ Chotka, Uttam Das, ...

accused_gender.quote: Accused Ganesh, in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
accused_gender.reason: All accused are men, referred to with male pronouns throughout.

accused_age.reason: No age is given for any accused in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: Religion of accused is not mentioned.

accused_caste.reason: Caste of accused is not mentioned.

accused_occupation.reason: Occupations are given for witnesses and the driver, not for the accused.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Socioeconomic status of accused is not stated; 'poor strata' refers to witnesses.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No previous criminal record is mentioned.

victim_age.reason: The judgment gives no age for the deceased.

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Known to deceased; accused repeatedly visited his house demanding money and threatened him
accused_victim_relationship.quote: the accused persons had also visited the house of Archideb several times for demanding money
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Accused were acquainted with and extorting the deceased, not strangers.

offence_category.reason: Offence is murder under s.302 IPC with related offences.

statutory_provisions.quote: charged under ss. 302, 201, 379, 411 rlw. s. 34 IPC
statutory_provisions.reason: Provisions match the charges as stated.

weapon.correct_value: Sharp cutting weapon (chopper recovered); gumcha used for strangulation
weapon.quote: recovery of the chopper which was recovered on the statement of accused Bishu
weapon.reason: Omits the chopper's identification and the gumcha used for strangulation.

evidence_type.quote: This is not purely a case of circumstantial evidence. There are eye-witnesses
evidence_type.reason: Circumstantial, eyewitness, medical and recovery evidence are all relied upon.

confession.correct_value: Accused Bishu admitted in custody that they had cut the body with the chopper, leading to recovery
confession.quote: admitted that they had cut the body of the deceased with the chopper
confession.reason: Judgment records an admission by an accused, contradicting 'None'.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: absconding of the accused not only goes with the hypothesis of guilt ... points a definite finger towards them
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Absconding, disposal of body, weapon use and multiple accused are all relied upon.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: No mitigating circumstances are discussed in the judgment.

trial_court_outcome.quote: Trial Court awarded sentence of death to all the accused persons
trial_court_outcome.reason: Trial court convicted all and imposed death sentence.

high_court_outcome.quote: acquitted all the accused persons of the offence under Section 379 read with Section 34 IPC
high_court_outcome.reason: Matches High Court's modification and life sentence with fine.

final_outcome.reason: Convictions upheld by the Supreme Court.

offence_finally_established.quote: the accused are responsible for commission of the murder of the deceased

imprisonment_type.quote: awarded them rigorous imprisonment for life
imprisonment_type.reason: Death sentence was replaced by life imprisonment on appeal; death is not the final sentence.

imprisonment_years.reason: Life term has no fixed years; null is consistent.

fine_rs.correct_value: Rs. 5,000 each (High Court), default two years rigorous imprisonment
fine_rs.quote: to pay a fine of Rs.5,000/- each in default to undergo rigorous imprisonment for two years each
fine_rs.reason: Judgment states a fine of Rs. 5,000 each, not null.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Facts only; remove court's conclusions that the chain was proved and absconding supports prosecution
neutral_facts.quote: The prosecution has proved the complete chain of events
neutral_facts.reason: Facts are accurate, but final sentences state the court's conclusions, which neutral facts must not reveal.

offence_severity.correct_value: Life imprisonment under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC (High Court); s.201 seven years RI upheld; s.379 acquitted
offence_severity.quote: sentencing the accused to life imprisonment
offence_severity.reason: Life term relates to s.302, not s.379; s.379 conviction was set aside.

attempt_completion.quote: the deceased was strangulated by the accused persons
attempt_completion.reason: Murder was completed; body was killed and disposed of.

physical_harm.quote: The cause of death was due to effect of strangulation by ligature
physical_harm.reason: Strangulation and mutilation of the body are documented.

number_of_offences.correct_value: Charged under four provisions; s.302 and s.201 upheld, s.379 acquitted by High Court
number_of_offences.quote: acquitted all the accused persons of the offence under Section 379 read with Section 34 IPC
number_of_offences.reason: Only two convictions were upheld; the s.379 conviction was set aside, not three.

financial_property_loss.correct_value: Deceased's rings, HMT watch and cash involved; cycle recovered; charges under ss.379 and 411 IPC
financial_property_loss.quote: four rings, HMT watch and was carrying cash and other papers
financial_property_loss.reason: Property loss is implicated by theft and receiving charges, so 'not applicable' understates it.

premeditation_planning.correct_value: Repeated demands and threats, including a threat on 27 Sept 2003 to murder him if money not paid; no express premeditation finding
premeditation_planning.quote: if their demand of Rs.40,000/- was not fulfilled within one day, they would murder him
premeditation_planning.reason: Prior threats to murder are described, so 'Not stated' is incomplete.

motive.quote: illegal demand of money coupled with the warning of dire consequences
motive.reason: Motive is the demand of Rs.40,000 for shop construction.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: the recoveries of the weapon of offence as well as the vehicle
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Accepted evidence matches the judgment's reasoning.

witness_credibility.quote: These witnesses are reliable and trustworthy.
witness_credibility.reason: Court found eye-witnesses reliable; hostile witnesses partially supported prosecution.

post_offence_conduct.quote: The accused persons were absconding immediately after the date of the occurrence
post_offence_conduct.reason: Absconding after the incident is recorded.

custody_duration.reason: Duration of accused custody is not stated.

trial_duration.correct_value: Offence 29/30 Sept 2003; trial judgment 13 Sept 2005; High Court 5 Feb 2007; Supreme Court 11 July 2012
trial_duration.reason: Trial judgment date is stated, contradicting 'Not stated'.

legal_representation.reason: Counsel names are listed but their roles for accused or State are not stated.

investigation_status.quote: Charge sheet against all other six accused was filed.
investigation_status.reason: FIR, charge sheet and completed trial are all recorded.

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Investigation lapses: no FSL sending of gunny bags/weapons, no site plan or shop photographs; delays in recording witness statements
procedural_irregularity.quote: the Investigating Officer failed to send the blood stained gunny bags and other recovered weapons to the FSL
procedural_irregularity.reason: Judgment notes investigative lapses and delay, contradicting 'None noted'.

appeal_history.reason: Trial, High Court and Supreme Court stages are accurately summarised.

prosecution_argument.quote: there are eye-witnesses to different events that had taken place
prosecution_argument.reason: Summary matches the State's arguments as recorded.

defence_argument.quote: the case being a case of circumstantial evidence does not complete chain of events
defence_argument.reason: Main defence contentions are accurately summarised.

legal_principle_applied.quote: two factors must be established i.e. common intention and participation
legal_principle_applied.reason: Section 34 principles and spur-of-moment common intention are correctly stated.

precedent_relied_upon.correct_value: Also cited: Nand Kishore, Banti alias Guddu, State of U.P. v. Satish, Sheo Shankar Singh, Maruti Rama Naik, State of Orissa v. Brahmananda Nanda, Munshi Singh Gautam, Jai Bhagwan; Govindaraju cited as (2012) 4 SCC 122 in text
precedent_relied_upon.quote: Nand Kishore v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2011) 12 SCC 120
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Several authorities relied on or referred to are omitted from the list.

sentencing_rationale.correct_value: No separate sentencing reasoning; Court affirmed High Court's life sentence, reasoning is on conviction and absconding
sentencing_rationale.quote: the prosecution has been able to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt
sentencing_rationale.reason: Reasons given relate to conviction, not a separate rationale for the final sentence.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: No mitigating factors are identified by the court.

judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: the accused were present at the scene of occurrence and participated in the crime
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Conduct, weapon/vehicle recoveries and presence at scene are relied upon.

other_sentence_order.correct_value: Trial court: seven years RI and Rs. 5,000 fine for s.201; three years RI and Rs. 1,000 fine for s.379 (later set aside); High Court maintained s.201 sentence
other_sentence_order.quote: For the offence under Section 201 IPC, they were sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of seven years
other_sentence_order.reason: Other sentences for s.201 and s.379 were imposed, contradicting 'None'.
